note: One composite index, as three different tools report it. Observed 2026-08-15 against a standard Firestore-native database, for issue #20 — before this, every reconcile test fed the module a listing the module's own author wrote. Verbatim except for the project id, which is the placeholder `demo-fixtures` rather than the disposable project actually used, matching `scripts/capture-fixtures.mjs`; nothing here reads the project segment, so the substitution costs no observation. Only the creation command is recorded below — how each rendering was read back is not, so this cannot yet be regenerated end to end.

source.project: demo-fixtures (placeholder; the observation was made against a disposable project)
source.declared: created with no density: `gcloud firestore indexes composite create --collection-group probe --field-config field-path=x,order=ascending --field-config field-path=z,order=ascending`

observations.densityIsAlwaysStamped: An index created with no density comes back SPARSE_ALL, and so does one created with --density density-unspecified: the API normalises rather than echoing. DENSITY_UNSPECIFIED was never returned. Re-observed 2026-08-23: the group created as density-unspecified still lists as SPARSE_ALL.
observations.enumsAreStrings: v1.FirestoreAdminClient returns state, density, apiScope and queryScope as enum names, identically over gRPC and over `fallback: true`. Not numbers, which `readiness.ts` warns the generated protos can deliver. Re-observed 2026-08-23 through the adapter, on all three indexes.
observations.sparseAnyAndDenseAreUnreachableHere: `--density sparse-any` and `--density dense` are refused at creation: 'Indexes with api scope ANY_API does not support SPARSE_ANY density on standard database'. So SPARSE_ALL is the only density a standard native database produces.
observations.uniqueIsEnterpriseOnly: `--unique` is refused: 'Unique index is only supported in the Enterprise database.' The field is still returned, as false.
observations.renderingsDiffer: Only the admin client fills in the fields holding their proto3 default — apiScope, unique, multikey, shardCount. gcloud omits them. That is why an absent apiScope has to count as comparable.
observations.wildcardListsEveryGroup: 2026-08-23, through `admin.ts` against the same disposable database: the parent `.../collectionGroups/-` returned every composite index in one call, across three different collection groups (probe, probe_sparse_all, probe_density_unspecified). This is the observation the adapter's design rests on — listing group by group would make the observed set a function of the corpus. Paging was not exercised: three entries is one page.
observations.searchIndexOptionsArrivesNull: The 2026-08-23 listing carried `searchIndexOptions: null`, which the 2026-08-15 one did not — the same client, eight days later. It is not modelled by `LiveCompositeIndex` and is not compared: it belongs to the MONGODB_COMPATIBLE_API scope that `COMPARABLE_API_SCOPES` already refuses, and null under ANY_API states nothing the canonical key could disagree with. What has not been observed is a non-null one under ANY_API, which would be the `unique`/`multikey`/`shardCount` hole of issue #30 by a fourth route.
